disclaimer: Example procedure, not an official NCPOR procedure.
description: Aurora's incident playbooks: one per failure type the twin can show (the public demo scenarios and the main alert and anomaly types). Read by simulator/assistant.py and served at GET /api/assistant/playbooks. Each one is a conservative EXAMPLE written for the demo: safety first, verify before acting, keep the station leader and the mainland informed. Typical causes are typical, never a diagnosis. Matching: an active demo scenario id wins; otherwise the playbook whose alert sensors match the incident's alerts (first in this file's order); otherwise its anomaly causes; otherwise 'anomaly'. Each step has `do` (the checklist text) and `say` (a short phrase for the spoken briefing). `baselineRisk` is the floor for this failure type (decision-engine scale nominal < low < moderate < high < critical): a briefing never states a lower risk, even while the engine has not caught up.

playbooks.title: Generator failure
playbooks.meaning: The primary diesel generator is producing less power than the station needs, or has stopped. Every building it powers is exposed, and the heating zones lose their electrical supply first.
typicalCauses: Fuel supply interruption (blocked filter, waxed fuel in extreme cold, empty day tank)
Engine protection trip (high coolant temperature, low oil pressure, overspeed)
Cooling system fault (coolant loss, radiator or fan failure)
Electrical fault on the alternator or the main switchboard
playbooks.affectedHint: Everything downstream of the Generator Shed in the dependency graph: both heating zones, water treatment, the comms tower, living quarters and the research lab.
playbooks.riskRationale: Loss of power removes heating within hours at Antarctic temperatures; frozen water lines and loss of communications follow. The time to restore power is the main driver of risk.

steps.do: Verify that backup power has taken over: standby generator running or UPS carrying the critical loads.
Check the affected electrical loads and shed non-essential ones so the standby supply is not overloaded.
Inspect the generator's fault indicators and alarm panel before any restart attempt; do not reset repeated trips.
Confirm heating is maintained in the living quarters and that water lines are protected from freezing.
steps.say: confirm heating in the living quarters

steps.do: Notify the station leader, log the event, and inform the mainland if power is not restored within the agreed time.

playbooks.title: Heating failure
playbooks.meaning: A heating zone is not delivering enough heat: supply temperature or flow is outside its normal range. The buildings it serves will cool down.
typicalCauses: Circulation pump failure or an air lock in the loop
Low system pressure from a leak
Boiler or heat-exchanger fault, or loss of waste heat from the generator
Control valve or thermostat fault
playbooks.affectedHint: The buildings the heating zone serves in the dependency graph (living quarters for zone A, the research lab for zone B).
playbooks.riskRationale: Indoor temperature falls quickly when the outside is far below freezing; crew safety and frozen pipes are the main risks. Risk rises with the outside cold and the time without heat.

steps.do: Check the indoor temperature in the affected buildings and move crew to a heated area if it keeps falling.
Verify the circulation pump is running and the loop pressure is within its normal range.
steps.say: verify the circulation pump and loop pressure

steps.do: Look for leaks along the heating loop and isolate any leaking section.
steps.say: look for leaks in the heating loop

steps.do: Bring standby heating online for the affected zone if it is available.
Notify the station leader and log the event, with the indoor temperatures over time.

playbooks.title: Water system alert
playbooks.meaning: The water treatment plant reports a low tank level or water quality outside its normal range (pH or temperature).
typicalCauses: Snow-melt production lower than consumption (melter fault or a heating shortfall)
Leak in the storage tank or distribution lines
Treatment dosing fault that changes the pH
Frozen intake or distribution line
playbooks.affectedHint: The buildings the water treatment plant supplies in the dependency graph (living quarters and the research lab).
playbooks.riskRationale: Drinking and sanitation water are essential; water outside its quality range must not be drunk until it has been checked again.

steps.do: Restrict drinking water use until the water quality has been checked by hand.
Verify the level reading with a manual check of the tank.
steps.say: verify the tank level by hand

steps.do: Inspect the snow melter, pumps and lines for leaks or freezing.
steps.say: inspect the melter, pumps and lines

steps.do: Check the treatment dosing and correct it only per the plant's own procedure.
Notify the station leader and start water rationing if the level keeps falling.

playbooks.title: CO₂ build-up in the living quarters
playbooks.meaning: Carbon dioxide in the living quarters is above its threshold, which usually means the air is not being exchanged fast enough.
typicalCauses: Ventilation fan failure or a blocked air intake (snow or ice)
Too many people in a closed space for the ventilation rate
Combustion source indoors (heater or cooking equipment)
playbooks.affectedHint: The living quarters, and the crew inside it.
playbooks.riskRationale: High CO₂ causes headaches and poor judgement; very high levels are dangerous. A combustion source can also mean carbon monoxide, which this twin does not measure.

steps.do: Move people out of the affected rooms if anyone has a headache or dizziness, or the level keeps rising.
steps.say: move people out if anyone feels unwell

steps.do: Check carbon monoxide with a handheld detector, since a combustion source is possible.
steps.say: check carbon monoxide with a handheld detector

steps.do: Verify the ventilation fans are running and the air intakes are not blocked by snow or ice.
steps.say: verify the ventilation fans and air intakes

steps.do: Increase fresh-air exchange and reduce occupancy until the level falls.
Notify the station leader and log the readings.

playbooks.title: Blizzard
playbooks.meaning: Wind, temperature or pressure outside the station has crossed storm thresholds. Visibility and outdoor safety drop, and the satellite link may degrade.
typicalCauses: A low-pressure system passing over the station
Katabatic winds from the ice sheet
playbooks.affectedHint: Outdoor operations, the comms tower (satellite link) and the heating load, which rises with wind and cold.
playbooks.riskRationale: Outdoor movement becomes dangerous in high wind and low visibility; external equipment can be damaged; communications may be lost.

steps.do: Stop outdoor work and account for everyone: confirm all personnel are inside.
steps.say: stop outdoor work and account for everyone

steps.do: Secure external equipment and close outer doors and hatches.
Check the heating and generator margin for the extra load from wind and cold.
steps.say: check the heating and generator margin

steps.do: Prepare for reduced satellite bandwidth: send critical messages early.
Notify the station leader and keep a weather watch until the wind drops.

playbooks.title: Satellite link loss
playbooks.meaning: The station's satellite link is down or badly degraded. The station keeps recording, but the mainland cannot see it until the link returns.
typicalCauses: Antenna misalignment or icing
Weather attenuation during a storm
Modem or power fault at the comms tower
Outage at the satellite operator
playbooks.affectedHint: The comms tower and every data stream to the mainland; on-site systems keep running.
playbooks.riskRationale: Without the link the station cannot ask for help or report status. Risk grows with the outage length and with any other incident running at the same time.

steps.do: Switch to the backup communication channel (HF radio or a secondary satellite terminal).
steps.say: switch to the backup communication channel

steps.do: Check power and status lights at the comms tower and the modem.
steps.say: check power at the comms tower

steps.do: Inspect the antenna for icing or misalignment when it is safe to go outside.
steps.say: inspect the antenna when it is safe

steps.do: Keep logging station data locally so nothing is lost while the link is down.
Agree a check-in schedule with the mainland on the backup channel and notify the station leader.
steps.say: agree a check-in schedule with the mainland

playbooks.title: Low fuel
playbooks.meaning: Fuel autonomy is lower than its threshold: either the stock is low or the generator is burning fuel faster than normal.
typicalCauses: Higher consumption from cold weather or a heavy load
Fuel leak or an unmetered loss
Reading error in the tank gauge
Resupply delay
playbooks.affectedHint: The generator and everything it powers, over the coming days.
playbooks.riskRationale: Fuel is the station's only primary energy source; running out stops power and heating. The days of autonomy left decide how urgent this is.

steps.do: Verify the fuel stock with a manual dip of the tanks.
steps.say: verify the fuel stock by hand

steps.do: Check for leaks along the fuel lines and around the storage area.
Reduce non-essential loads to lower the burn rate.
Recalculate days of autonomy with the measured stock and the current burn.
Notify the station leader and the mainland logistics team about the resupply timing.
steps.say: notify the station leader and mainland logistics

playbooks.title: Unexplained anomaly
playbooks.meaning: The anomaly detector reports readings that differ from what the physics model expects, and they do not match a known failure signature.
typicalCauses: Sensor fault or drift
An early-stage equipment fault
An operating condition the physics model does not include
playbooks.affectedHint: The buildings of the sensors that deviate most from the physics prediction.
playbooks.riskRationale: An unexplained deviation is a reason to check, not proof of a fault. The detector compares against synthetic prototype signatures, not a validated diagnosis.

steps.do: Read the anomaly evidence: which sensors deviate from the physics prediction, and by how much.
Verify the deviating readings with a second instrument or a visual check.
Inspect the equipment behind those sensors for visible faults.
steps.say: inspect the equipment behind those sensors

steps.do: Notify the station leader if the deviation grows or a threshold alert follows.
steps.say: notify the station leader if it grows
